grass.animatedNote: Only tall-grass and flower tiles sway; plain grass stays still. Draw the -sway sheet in place of the still tile and start each tile at frame (col+row) % 4 so a soft wind wave rolls across the meadow.

litter.note: darker grass with fallen leaves; used where maps/town.json groundStyle says "litter" (under thick groves)

mixes.rule: each grass tile uses the mix named by maps/town.json groundStyle ("" = default); pick the category by weight, then a file at random (seeded)

overlays.rule: draw tile-water, then for every land neighbour draw the matching overlay on top. Edges use the 4 side neighbours; a corner overlay only when that diagonal is land and both sides next to it are water.

water.variantNote: 4 variants x 4 frames (128x16 sheets, 32x16 frames). Pick a variant per tile at random (seeded) so the river does not show a grid; all tiles share one frame clock so the ripples flow together. Ripples stay inside the diamond, so any variants can sit side by side.

slums.note: The Slums' ground (maps/slums.json). ground: floor tiles per kind, 32x16, anchor = diamond centre; pick a variant per tile, seeded by col,row. canal: a 4-frame strip on a shared clock, banks from tiles.water's overlays. Raised ground (tiles/slums/slums-elevation-README.md): one level = 16 px; cliffs, rim, cap and ramps are 32x32 pieces anchored on the diamond centre of the tile they stand on (16,24). cliffs: <material>.l / .r = the wall shown when the SW / SE neighbour is lower (one per level of drop, 16 px apart), variant seeded by col,row. rim nw/ne: outline on a raised top whose NW / NE neighbour is lower. cap w/e: corner edges. ramps: <surface>.<dir> = [part 1 (low cell), part 2], dir = the way you walk up.
slums.highTerrainNote: High terrain (tiles/slums/slums-high-terrain-README.md): ground void (a chasm floor, below level 0) and cracked (walkable); cliffs rock and scrap with `lower` (every step below the top one), chasm (one level below the ground) and chasm-deep (two); foot l/r = the line on a wall's lowest step; lip nw/ne = the chasm lip in place of the rim next to a void. PLACEHOLDER art until the art folder has its own (scripts/terrain/placeholders.ts).

palengke.note: The Lumang Palengke's ground (maps/palengke.json; the art folder's tiles/palengke, rows in its _sheets.csv). ground: floor tiles per family, 32x16, anchor = diamond centre; a variant per tile by a well-mixed hash of col,row seeded per family, the first `plainVariants` (the plain ones) `plainWeight` times as likely as the detailed ones. animated: families whose files are 4-frame strips (128x16) at fps on a shared clock, drawn as sprites over the baked ground: baha (shallow flood, walkable at `slow` of the speed) and lalim (deep pools, blocked, with tiles.water's bank overlays where they meet other ground: `banks`). The map is flat, so no cliffs, rims, caps, ramps.

silong.note: Ang Silong's floors (maps/silong-b1..b3.json, built by scripts/build-silong.ts; the art folder's silong/ (20 Oct 2026), rows in its _sheets.csv). ground: floor tiles per family, 32x16, anchor = diamond centre, the first `plainVariants` of each family `plainWeight` times as likely; walltop = the tops of the walls ('#', 2 levels up); cliffs.wall: the wall faces (32x32, anchor 16,24) stacked like the Slums' cliff faces; rim and cap borrow the Slums' (the art folder has none for the Silong); animated: the conveyor belts (4-frame strips on the shared clock); elevator-arrive / elevator-down: the elevators' floor plates (stand-ins under the PixelLab cage).

wardrobe.keys: MAIN ramp (DCDCF0,A8A8C8,74749A,48486A) = the item's main colour; TRIM ramp (F0E0C8,C0A888,8A7258) = its accent (stripes, jacket inner shirt, polo collar, cargo pockets, all shoe colours); FBEEE9 = sneaker sole (never swapped)

wardrobe.hairNote: All 8 dirs, all anims (rot, walk, idle, sit, wave, cheer). Hair ramp keys E8E8E8,B4B4B4,7C7C7C,4A4A4A; navy outline 1E1B3A. long and ponytail already sit behind the body below the neck in side views. mohawk leaves the sides bald by design.
wardrobe.hatNote: Hats are recoloured on the MAIN ramp (DCDCF0,A8A8C8,74749A,48486A). beanie and cap ship a clip mask per frame: white pixels = hide the hair layer there (erase hair under the hat) before drawing the hat. ribbon has no clip mask and hides no hair. When a clipping hat is worn with 'buns', draw 'crop' instead (hatHairFallback). Cosmetic hats (cosmeticHats: item id → hat key, the Lamp-head Hat's lamp) are never in hats: the creator, the Parlor, randomOutfit and the NPCs never offer them; only wearing the item puts one on a look. fixedColourHats use their own colours (no hat ramp swap). litHats ship a hatlit sheet per frame (hatLitPattern: the glass and bulb only), drawn untinted over the doll at night with litGlow (fx) centred on the glass, offset px below the head's top. A hat with a hatCanvas entry (the Witch Hat's witch) is drawn from a bigger cell (size) with the doll's 32x48 cell at offset inside it: each frame goes at the doll's position less offset; its clip masks stay 32x48, zero offset. Hats without an entry are 32x48 at zero offset. Head cosmetics' hats draw over the hair like any other hat, so long hair still shows below them (Mac, 17 Oct 2026): the lamp clips it with its masks; the witch doesn't (hatClips false: the art folder's char-hatclip-witch-* masks are solid white, made when head cosmetics hid all the hair; its big hat drawn over the head covers what it should). The store's Sets' hats (19 Oct 2026: nightwing, emberimp, gremlin, gravecaller, sylph) are 64x64 hatCanvas hats with the doll's cell at (16, 16), fixed colours, no clip: drawn over the hair like the witch's.
wardrobe.cosmeticPoseNote: A top in cosmeticPoseTops has a sheet fitted to every combat pose (cosmeticPosePattern: each class, anim and direction of classes.list, 64x64 cells in the pose's own cell, the pose body's frame count; the art folder's cosmetics/custom/poses), drawn over the pose's body in place of its idle top and topover; its shoes and bottom stay hidden, the hair and hat are laid on as for any look.
wardrobe.cosmeticTopsNote: Cosmetic tops (cosmeticTops: item id → top key, the Witch Robe's witchrobe): a worn body cosmetic draws characters/layers/top/char-top-<key>-* in the top's place in its own colours (no ramp swap); one in cosmeticHidesBottom covers the legs, so the bottom layer isn't drawn while it's worn (shoes still are). One in cosmeticHidesShoes draws its own feet, so the shoes aren't drawn either; one in topCanvas also has a topover sheet (topOverPattern, a bigger cell with the doll's at offset, like hatCanvas) holding only what reaches past the doll's cell (wings, tails, a wide hem), drawn whole just above the doll; one in cosmeticBodyClip ships a 32x48 mask per frame (bodyClipPattern): white = the body layer isn't drawn there (the Velvet Nightwing floats with no legs). Never in top: the creator, the Parlor, randomOutfit and the NPCs never offer them, and a saved look never holds one.

classes.note: The six classes (data: classes/classes.json). Combat poses per class and anim: for each direction the body, the face (s/se/e/sw/w) and the weapon layers behind (back, drawn before the body) and in front (front, after the body, face and clothes), in draw order. Weapon cells are 64x64 with the 32x48 body cell at bodyOffset (Slingshot's weapon is 32x48 like the body). All of it packs into one sheet of its own (scripts/packs.ts), loaded only once the event is on. Repo addition (Halloween 2026).

corner-small.note: small corner web, top-left corner at 0,0 (flip for other corners)

corner-medium.note: medium corner web, top-left corner at 0,0

corner-large.note: big corner web with a resting spider, top-left corner at 0,0

drape-long.note: long sagging web strung between two points at 0,1 and 39,1

drape-very-long.note: very long droopy web between two points at 0,1 and 71,1, with a hanging wrapped bug

orb.note: round orb web, hang it by its top middle (12,0)

orb-big-spider.note: big orb web with a spider waiting in the middle, hang by top middle (20,0)

torn.note: old torn orb web with a big hole and loose strands, hang by top middle (14,0)

strands.note: loose hanging wisps, tie the top edge to a branch or eave

spider-house.note: full spider house: a dense tangle of webs with a funnel nest, egg sacks, wrapped bugs and three spiders; top edge ties to a roof or branch
